chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man places his male organ upon the woman’s private part and ejaculates; is ghusl obligatory upon her? He said: If any of the fluid reaches her, then she should wash it off, and there is nothing due upon her unless he penetrates. I said: Then if she reaches climax but he does not penetrate? He said: Ghusl is not obligatory upon her.

key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the emitted fluid referred to in the ruling
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath that becomes obligatory in certain states of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl if there is ejaculation without penetration?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ghusl in a case where there is external sexual contact without penetration. It states that mere contact and even her climax, without penetration, do not obligate ghusl upon the woman, though any fluid reaching her should be washed away.
